title: Holy orders
hook: deacons, priests and bishops ordained by the laying on of hands

segments.voice: Yesterday, the anointing of the sick. Your line was the sick are not forgotten. Who did you call or keep in mind? Day one hundred thirty-one.

At one point in an ordination Mass, a young man in a white robe walks to the front of a packed cathedral and lies down. Flat on the floor, face down, arms at his sides. The whole congregation kneels and sings a long list of saints' names, asking each one to pray for him. It goes on for minutes. His mother is usually in tears. It's one of the most startling things you'll see in a Catholic church: a person giving his whole body to the ground before he's given a job. Today's word: ordination.
screen: `A YOUNG MAN LIES FACE DOWN.` → `A LONG LIST OF SAINTS.` → `HIS WHOLE BODY TO THE GROUND.`

segments.voice: Ordination comes from the Latin ordo, an order or rank, the word Romans used for the groups that made up their society. The sacrament is called holy orders, plural, because there are three: deacons, priests and bishops. The names are Greek. Deacon is diakonos, a servant, someone who waits on tables. Priest comes, through old English, from presbyteros, an elder. And bishop comes from episkopos, an overseer. Each one is a kind of serving. The sign is very old: hands laid on the head in silence. In the book of Acts, seven men are chosen to care for widows, whom Catholic tradition counts as the first deacons, and in the Douay-Rheims, "they praying, imposed hands upon them." The letters to Timothy also recall a gift that came through the laying on of hands. At an ordination today, the bishop lays his hands on the candidate's head without a word, then prays the prayer of consecration. At a priest's ordination, every priest present comes up and lays on hands too. Catholics believe this sacrament, like baptism, marks a person for good. Priests celebrate the Eucharist and hear confessions; deacons baptize, preach, witness marriages and serve the poor; bishops lead a diocese and ordain others. In the Latin Church, priests and bishops are normally celibate, while permanent deacons can be married, and Eastern Catholic churches have married priests. The Church ordains only men, and teaches it has no authority to do otherwise; some Catholics hope that will change. Other Christians understand ministry differently: the Orthodox keep the same three orders, while most Protestant churches ordain ministers but don't count ordination as a sacrament.
screen: `ORDO: AN ORDER, A RANK.` · `SERVANT, ELDER, OVERSEER.` · `HANDS LAID ON IN SILENCE.` · `MARKED FOR GOOD, TO SERVE.` · then, large: `CALLED TO SERVE.`

segments.voice: Here's the practice: remember a priest, deacon or minister you've known. Settle, and breathe. Maybe the one who baptized you, or buried your grandmother, or just said something kind after a service. If you don't know one, think of anyone whose job is to look after others: a nurse, a teacher, a coach. See their face. Think about how tired they might be. If you pray, you can pray for them by name. If you don't, just wish them well. The bell holds the time.
Ordination. From the Latin for an order. Deacons, priests and bishops, made by the laying on of hands to serve. Today's word.
Your line: called to serve. Today, thank one person who serves you, a priest, a pastor, a nurse, a bus driver, out loud and by name. Day one hundred thirty-one.

howItsDone: Catholic deacons, priests and bishops are ordained by a bishop, usually in a cathedral, through the silent laying on of hands and a prayer of consecration, after years of formation.
